headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: slim has broad shell/filesystem/network powers while nuwa-skill is a non-runnable docs-only skill with allowlisted egress, so interaction risks are mostly indirect and bounded.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, and nuwa-skill is non-runnable, so direct injection is not evidenced. slim can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, so if an operator manually copies nuwa-skill output into slim, prompt-like content could influence commands. This is a low-risk manual bridge, not a default pathway.
conditions: IF an operator manually pastes nuwa-skill output into slim's interactive prompt, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared file is used as a handoff between the agents, file-based instruction hijacking becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting model output into slim prompts.
Use a fixed handoff template that strips instructions.
Review any shared file before slim reads it.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress and no touched data classes are listed, while slim touches filesystem artifacts, certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials. There is no documented shared workspace or direct data bridge, so leakage is not default. The main risk is operator-mediated transfer of sensitive slim artifacts into nuwa-skill outputs.
conditions: IF slim artifacts are copied into nuwa-skill prompts or logs, sensitive data can leak.
IF both agents are pointed at the same secret-bearing directory, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not expose private keys or registry credentials to nuwa-skill.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Redact secrets before any handoff.
Disable verbose logging around slim runs.
requires-engineering: enforce secret-scanning on shared artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: slim has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and broad network egress; nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress. Even without a shared lock or shared-state claim, both can act on the same external resources if orchestrated together, creating overlapping write/side-effect potential. Uncertainty about the absent concurrency model pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same filesystem path, write conflicts become possible.
IF both agents are allowed to mutate the same external service or registry, side effects can collide.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize access to shared resources.
Run one agent at a time for mutable targets.
Use read-only mounts where possible.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: slim is an interactive CLI that executes commands, so if it consumes nuwa-skill output as authoritative guidance, errors can cascade into real actions. nuwa-skill is a research skill with allowlisted egress, but no verification or critique loop is documented. The pair therefore supports an A-to-B handoff that can propagate mistakes in default operator workflows.
conditions: IF slim is instructed to execute commands derived from nuwa-skill output, cascading errors become actionable.
IF nuwa-skill output is treated as ground truth without human review, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before execution.
Separate analysis from execution steps.
Ask slim to summarize commands before running them.
Use dry-run mode where available.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and no PHI/PII class is explicitly listed. slim does handle secrets and filesystem artifacts, but nuwa-skill has no declared sensitive-data handling. With only docs-level evidence, compliance risk is limited to ordinary operational handling rather than a specific policy breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into slim's workspace and then forwarded to nuwa-skill, policy review is needed.
IF the deployment imposes retention or residency rules not reflected in the profiles, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared handoffs.
Document retention for slim outputs.
Review secret-handling procedures.
Use separate storage for each agent.
requires-engineering: map data flows to policy controls.
